transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-09-29 14:00 UTC
- Duration: 43 minutes (recording)
- Attendees: Alex Romero (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Havenbrook Sec Eng), Priya Nair (CTO), Ethan Cruz (Infra)

Summary:
Havenbrook is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing document summarization and an internal RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) pipeline. Primary gating items: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO (SAML) and SCIM support, KMS integration (bring-your-own-key), audit-log retention/forwarding, RBAC and org-level separation, and options for private/VPC or on-prem deployments for high-sensitivity workloads. They want a clear path: start with hosted for dev/proof-of-concept, move to Dedicated for production, and keep Private/on-prem as a possibility for regulated datasets.

Topics covered:
- Compliance evidence (SOC2, ISO27001) and timeline to provide artifacts
- SSO/SAML, SCIM, SSO lifecycle, IdP compatibility
- RBAC: roles, token scoping, org/team separation
- Audit logs and export/retention options (SIEM integration)
- Encryption and KMS: BYOK, HSM integrations, key rotation
- Data retention and deletion SLA for logs and payloads
- Hosting options: Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private (VPC/on-prem) and migration path
- Performance/latency considerations for Dedicated vs Hosted

Action items (recap at end): see metadata fields above.

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect at times):
[00:00] Alex (AE): Ok hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Alex from Redwood, with Samir and Maya — we'll run through security intake and hosting options. Jordan, Priya, Ethan, thanks for making time.
[00:14] Jordan (Havenbrook): Yep hi, thanks. We're short on time so I put the most important bullets in the calendar invite: SOC2 evidence, SSO, KMS and logging.
[00:22] Priya (CTO): And to add, we need clear path for staging to prod, and whether we can push really sensitive PII pipelines off-hosted into our VPC.
[00:30] Samir (SE): Totally makes sense. Quick question on scope — are you planning to start with a customer-facing summarization feature, or internal first?
[00:38] Ethan (Infra): Both, but customer-facing is the blocker. We have regulated customers so the compliance bit is make or break.
[00:45] Alex: Understood. On SOC2, we can share our latest Type II report and a summary pack. Just to call out, we host a public security hub — I'll send links after the call.
[00:55] Jordan: When you say "share" — is that the full report or an executive summary? We typically need the auditor's detail and evidence of controls for higher tier customers.
[01:03] Maya (SE): We can provide the full auditor report under an NDA. The public summary covers scope and our controls; the detailed report includes test results and control mapping.
[01:12] Jordan: Ok, we'll need the detailed. Also ISO?
[01:15] Samir: We're ISO27001 certified as well, yes. We have scope docs.
[01:20] Priya: Great — please include the certificate and the scope so our compliance team can map it.
[01:25] Jordan: Next, SSO — we use Okta, but also have some customers on Azure AD. Any gotchas with SAML?
[01:33] Samir: We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning; Okta and Azure AD are both in our tested IdP list. FYI sometimes the metadata exchange trips up on clock skew — small retry.
[01:44] Ethan: On provisioning: we want automatic team provisioning & deprovisioning, and token revocation on user delete.
[01:52] Maya: SCIM handles provisioning; tokens are bound to service identities. We surface token revocation APIs and sessions in the admin console. We'll include docs.
[01:59] Jordan: Do you have RBAC at team and org levels? We need separation between the product team and security team access.
[02:06] Samir: Yes, role-based access with custom roles via the console and API. You can scope models, routes, and datasets per team. We also support audit log filtering by org.
[02:16] Priya: About audit logs — we need to ship logs to our SIEM (Splunk) and retain them for seven years for certain regulated workflows. Can you forward?
[02:26] Alex: We can forward audit logs via an encrypted syslog or S3 export. Default retention on hosted is 90 days, but for enterprise Dedicated/Private we support longer retention or custom retention policies. Exports can be continuous.
[02:38] Jordan: Is that configurable per route or per org?
[02:41] Samir: It's configurable at the org level and can be filtered per service route. For example you can forward only admin events to SIEM or everything.
[02:50] Ethan: We also want immutable logs or at least tamper-evident logs for audit.
[02:55] Maya: We support append-only log storage and signed log exports; for Private deployments you can use your own WORM storage. We'll detail options.
[03:05] Priya: Encryption: BYOK is a requirement for our highest-sensitivity set. Can you integrate with our AWS KMS and support HSM-backed keys?
[03:13] Samir: Yes — BYOK is supported in Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports envelope encryption with keys we manage, but we also support customer-managed keys in KMS for Dedicated. HSM integrations are available in Private offering.
[03:25] Jordan: Key rotation — how often, and lineage?
[03:28] Samir: We don't rotate customer keys for BYOK; the customer controls rotation in their KMS. We support key version metadata in audit logs so you have lineage.
[03:36] Ethan: For hosted, if we send PII in prompts, what's Redwood's retention policy? Do you store prompt/response traces?
[03:45] Alex: For hosted public API, by default we retain for 30 days for safety and debugging, but we can turn off retention for enterprise contracts; for Dedicated/Private we don't retain customer payloads by default. We'll share the exact retention SLA.
[03:57] Jordan: So to clarify — hosted default: 30 days; enterprise/Dedicated: configurable/no retention; Private: none.
[04:04] Maya: Correct, and we can set auto-delete policies and provide deletion APIs plus an attestable deletion log.
[04:10] Priya: About data-in-transit and at-rest, tls level and ciphers?
[04:15] Samir: TLS1.2+ and we prefer TLS1.3; we can provide cipher suite list. At-rest encryption uses AES256. For BYOK we rely on your KMS provider.
[04:25] Jordan: Are transcripts / request payloads part of the audit trail — i.e., can we exclude them from logs?
[04:30] Maya: Yes you can mask or redact fields before storage, or not persist payloads at all for certain routes. We'll show how to configure masking rules.
[04:39] Ethan: Network topology: if we go Dedicated in your cloud, will traffic ever cross public endpoints? We need VPC peering or PrivateLink.
[04:47] Samir: Dedicated can be deployed in a customer VPC with PrivateLink, VPC peering, or our managed VPCs. We support static egress IPs and strict egress controls.
[04:56] Priya: And for on-prem — what's the installer? We run Kubernetes on-prem and sometimes air-gapped clusters.
[05:02] Alex: Private on-prem package is available; it's a containerized stack with an operator. Air-gapped installs are supported; for the initial bootstrap we exchange manifests and signed artifacts. We'll share the installer checklist.
[05:13] Jordan: Ok great. Any SOC2 gaps you typically see customers ask about?
[05:18] Maya: Common ask is data residency mapping and vendor subservice mapping. Also documentation for change management and vulnerability scanning cadence. We have published policies and scan reports.
[05:28] Jordan: Regarding vulnerability scanning — do you publish SBOMs?
[05:31] Samir: We can provide SBOM extracts for the stack components for enterprise engagements.
[05:35] Ethan: Performance: once we go Dedicated, what's typical p95 latency for a 2k token completion on gpus you host?
[05:44] Samir: For the model sizes you mentioned we typically see 150–350ms per token on our optimized runtime depending on sequence length; end-to-end p95 for a 2k completion is often around 1.5–3s on Dedicated; hosted can be similar but depends on noisy neighbors — Dedicated gives more predictable tail latency.
[06:02] Priya: That sounds fine. Cost delta?
[06:05] Alex: We'll share a rough cost matrix. Dedicated has committed monthly cost but lower per-token compute; hosted is pay-as-you-go with premium on tail latencies. Samir will provide ballpark numbers.
[06:14] Jordan: Ok. About model variants: we want automatic fallback when capacity changes — e.g., fallback from large to medium model with same API.
[06:22] Samir: We support routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; you can set cost vs quality tradeoff rules.
[06:29] Priya: For compliance, we'll need to map Redwood controls to our internal control framework (SOC/ISO mapping doc). Do you have a control matrix?
[06:36] Alex: Yes, we'll include a control matrix (control id -> Redwood control mapping -> evidence location). We'll attach that to the pack.
[06:43] Jordan: Can we run a short PoC where we send 10k requests and validate retention/no-retention behavior, and run Splunk ingest of logs?
[06:50] Samir: Absolutely — we typically do a smoke test for logging and retention. We can spin up a sandbox Dedicated or use a hosted enterprise sandbox.
[06:58] Ethan: For the sandbox, what are the network prerequisites?
[07:01] Maya: For hosted sandbox it's simple — just IP allowlist and SAML. For Dedicated sandbox in your VPC, we'll need a peering config and some role-based IAM pieces. We'll send a checklist.
[07:12] Alex: Quick note on incident response — we have a published incident response playbook and will designate an escalation engineer for enterprise customers.
[07:21] Jordan: RTO/RPO — what's the SLA?
[07:24] Samir: Our Dedicated SLAs include uptime targets and RTO/RPO commitments; we'll include the SLA PDF. Hosted has uptime guarantees in our terms.
[07:33] Priya: A little about org structure — if we start hosted for POC but later go Dedicated, how smooth is the migration for keys, models and routing?
[07:43] Maya: We provide model version pinning and export tools for KV cache and model artifacts. Key migration for BYOK requires rewrapping tokens but we help with tooling. The main work is data egress and validating deleted stored payloads; we have migration runbooks.
[07:58] Ethan: When you say KV cache export — how do you handle cache privacy? We can't leak user prefixes.
[08:05] Samir: KV cache is per-tenant and encrypts entries; migration tooling writes directly to your target storage and doesn't leak to other tenants.
[08:13] Jordan: We also need to understand your subprocessor list — any third party logging or analytics vendors?
[08:19] Alex: We'll provide the current subprocessors; it's in the security pack; you can request removal or a tailored agreement for enterprise.
[08:27] Priya: One last technical — do you support tokenized redaction or deterministic redaction so we can track re-identified items?
[08:35] Maya: We have deterministic tokenization for PII redaction and can rehydrate under customer controls — will add doc links.
[08:41] Jordan: Anything we should be aware of re: exportable logs for audits?
[08:46] Samir: Audit exports include event types, actor, timestamp, IP, key version; payloads are optional. Exports are JSON-lines with signing metadata.
[08:56] Ethan: Ok can we confirm timeline — we need the SOC2 docs and KMS spec by EOD tomorrow ideally.
[09:03] Alex: We'll send the pack and the vendor questionnaire responses today, ideally within 24 hours.
[09:09] Jordan: We'll book the infra deep-dive for next week to run the PoC.
[09:12] Priya: Great.
[09:15] Alex: Recap: Alex to share SOC2/ISO and control matrix; Samir to send latency/cost matrix and PoC checklist; Maya to send installer checklist and SCIM/SAML guides. Jordan to share internal retention policy and sample volumes. We'll put next steps in the calendar.
[09:34] (crosstalk) Ethan: Thanks everyone.
[09:36] Alex: Thanks, bye.

Post-call notes:
- Links to attach in follow-up: security pack (SOC2 Type II PDF), ISO27001 cert, control mapping spreadsheet, SCIM/SAML quickstart, Private deployment installer checklist, Dedicated cost/latency matrix sample.
- Customer tone: serious, compliance-driven; likely to start with hosted sandbox then move to dedicated sandbox pending results.
- Risk flags: needs full SOC2 report under NDA, long-log retention requirements (7 years) could require custom retention clauses; air-gapped on-prem requirement possible for some regulated workloads.
